{
  "channel": "eng-ml",
  "thread_ts": "1766543210",
  "first_message_ts": "1766543210",
  "last_message_ts": "1766543600",
  "participants": [
    "sara",
    "liam",
    "mike",
    "eva",
    "ci-bot"
  ],
  "text": "sara: Quick heads-up — the scorecard histogram in the quant-compare diff view looks shifted after the latest quantization runs. Buckets are compressed, and the brush selects wrong ranges. Screenshot: https://files.redwood.dev/quant-hist.png :eyes:
liam: Reproduced. Happens on both real and synthetic evals. Seems worse for long-tail distributions. Is this just 4-bit/8-bit?
mike: I think it's not quant specific. Saw similar when we flipped the rollup aggregation to 'bucket_midpoint' in runner v2.4. The stored bucket keys changed.
sara: here's the query I ran locally to inspect counts:
```sql
SELECT bucket_key, count(*) as n
FROM eval_samples
WHERE run_id = '2026-05-28-quant-sweep'
GROUP BY bucket_key
ORDER BY bucket_key
```
ci-bot: CI pipeline rerun triggered for branch fix/histogram-domain (job #7821) :gear:
liam: My guess: frontend expects open-interval buckets [a,b) but runner now emits midpoint keys (a+b)/2. Chart.js stacking uses domain based on keys, brush uses original range endpoints -> off-by-half-bucket width.
eva: I dug into the transform. Confirmed: histogram component builds domain from sample.bin_edges when present, but the brush control falls back to computed domain from xScale.domain() which uses keys. If keys are midpoints, the brush snaps differently. Quick mitigation: prefer edges array over keys for brush domain. I'll open a small PR.
mike: Sounds right. Also check how quant-run exporter writes bin_edges vs keys; if exporter drops edges for memory we need to keep them for UI.
sara: Can you link the failing dashboard run and the PR once ready? This blocks the scorecard QA for quantized comparisons. :pray:
eva: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/ui/pulls/412 — adds edges->domain fallback + unit test for brush selection. CI job #7821 will run tests.
ci-bot: CI job #7821: tests passing on linux/amd64, failing on windows due to snapshot path issue.
liam: Nice. If CI is green I can update the runner exporter to always include bin_edges (cheap) and we avoid future mismatches.
sara: Perfect. Thanks everyone — assigning follow-ups: @eva push PR, @liam update runner exporter, @mike add a short e2e that loads quant-compare and checks brush selection stays within histogram bounds.
eva: on it, will ping when merged. :thumbsup:",

  "content_field_names": [
    "text"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_4d4a2a3844fa43d699b22e89b3433ea0"
}

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-582001\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Token-aggregation + prefetch: regression watch and robustness evaluation\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-22\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"creator\": \"Ava Martinez\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Rahul Patel\",\n  \"project\": \"Inference-Config-Health\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-31\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"evals\",\n    \"regression-monitoring\",\n    \"serving-runtime\",\n    \"kv-prefetch\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-611200\",\n    \"ENG-574000\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.22\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Goal: Build a repeatable eval and monitoring harness that detects subtle quality regressions introduced by token-aggregation (microbatching/aggregation heuristics) and KV-prefetch policies. We want to understand the functional cost (response divergence, hallucination rate, structured-output integrity) per unit latency saved across representative production slices and ensure safe rollout rules for config changes. Background: Recent runtime work introduced an aggressive token-aggregation mode that reduces per-request overhead by merging short concurrent requests and a KV-prefetch heuristic that proactively warms KV caches for long-running chat sessions. Early perf gains are promising, but there are anecdotal degradations on structured tasks (code, JSON-extraction) and on certain prompt fingerprints. This ticket scopes an evaluation plan, orchestration for long-running watches, alert thresholds, and a canary gating policy for config rollouts.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": \"1) We can run a 10k-sample slice-based evaluation within CI that reports per-slice latency delta and quality regression scores for any candidate config change. 2) An alerting rule is defined that trips when weighted quality delta > 2% and latency improvement < 10% or when any structured-output integrity test fails. 3) Canary gating automation (deploy blocked/rollback) implemented in the rollout pipeline using the harness. 4) Dashboard widgets and a single-run report template are added to the perf dashboard.\",\n  \"evaluation_metrics\": \"- latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, throughput_rps, avg_tokens_per_request\\n- quality_emd (earth mover distance) on distribution of n-gram overlaps for freeform outputs\\n- structured_integrity_pass_rate (JSON/CSV extraction tests)\\n- hallucination_rate (precision/recall against reference KG)\\n- semantic_similarity_mean (embedding cosine vs golden)\\n- per-slice_weighted_regression_score (custom weighted delta)\\n- stability_score (variance of outputs across repeated seeds)\",\n  \"test_datasets\": \"- prod-sampled-10k (anonymized production traces covering web/chat/agent)\\n- code-generation-promptset-1k (open-source)\\n- structured-extraction-500 (forms + receipts)\\n- conversational-long-context-2k\\n- adversarial-prompt-fingerprints-200 (synthesized edge cases)\",\n  \"methodology\": \"1) Baseline run: current stable config (runtime-1.21) across full dataset. 2) Candidate runs: token-aggregation at three aggressiveness levels and KV-prefetch enabled/disabled + two TTL settings. 3) For each run capture deterministic outputs by pinning model version & seed, collect latency traces with synthetic burst injection to emulate microbursts. 4) Compute per-slice metrics and produce a regression matrix (quality delta vs latency improvement). 5) Statistical significance: bootstrap per-slice with 1000 resamples; highlight regressions with p < 0.05 and effect size > threshold. 6) Produce human-review digest for any failing slices with example prompts and diffs.\",\n  \"monitoring_playbook\": \"- Alert tier-1: structured_integrity_pass_rate drops by >1 percentage point for any slice -> page oncall infra.\\n- Alert tier-2: per-slice_weighted_regression_score > 2% for >30min -> create auto-ticket and pause rollout.\\n- Rollback rule: if any structured_integrity test fails OR global weighted quality delta >3% during canary -> immediate automatic rollback and notify SRE + PM.\\n- Follow-up: if alert fires, run postmortem within 72 hours and quarantine failing prompt fingerprints into a protected testset.\",\n  \"orchestration_and_harness\": \"- Integrate eval job into CI pipeline (github actions) that can be triggered by config PRs.\\n- Long-running watches: scheduled job every 6 hours that runs lightweight sampled checks and reports to dashboard.\\n- Canary gating: deployment job calls the harness with canary sample (1% traffic equivalent) and will auto-block if alerts fire.\\n- Repro artifacts: store outputs, diffs, and metric snapshots in a date-stamped folder on GCS and link in report.\",\n  \"artifacts\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Token+Aggregation+Prefetch+Study\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298\",\n    \"https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/token-agg-prefetch-matrix\"\n  ],\n  \"checklist\": [\n    \"seed evaluation harness and sample runner\",\n    \"implement deterministic output capture (model version + seed)\",\n    \"define per-slice weighting scheme with PM\",\n    \"add structured-output unit tests\",\n    \"add alerts to ops-monitoring\",\n    \"hook canary gating into deploy pipeline\",\n    \"write runbook for oncall\"\n  ],\n  \"risks_and_mitigation\": \"- Risk: Small but high-impact regressions on rare prompt fingerprints may be masked by global averages. Mitigation: enforce per-slice thresholds and maintain adversarial fingerprint set.\\n- Risk: Increased monitoring load and storage. Mitigation: lightweight periodic checks + TTL on stored diffs.\\n- Risk: Flaky CI due to nondeterministic model IO. Mitigation: pin seeds and run small ensemble to estimate variance.\",\n  \"notes_or_decisions\": \"- Decided to prioritize structured-output integrity over marginal latency wins for enterprise tenants.\\n- We will treat KV-prefetch toggles as separate binary feature flags to allow independent rollback.\\n- Metric weighting will be: structured_integrity 40%, hallucination_rate 30%, semantic_similarity 20%, latency 10% (subject to PM signoff).\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-02-23 Ava Martinez: Initial scope drafted; shared with PM and SRE for feedback.\",\n    \"2026-02-26 Rahul Patel: Implemented deterministic capture prototype and small-run diffs; added synthetic microburst runner (PR linked).\",\n    \"2026-03-02 Priya Kaur (PM): Reviewed slice weighting proposal; suggested raising structured-output weight to 40% \\u2014 accepted.\",\n    \"2026-03-06 Jin Park (SRE): Added alert thresholds and will add Grafana dashboard panels; requested retention policy for diffs.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 Rahul Patel: Canary gating automation merged to staging; lightweight watch scheduled every 6 hours. document.title: Token-aggregation + prefetch: regression watch and robustness evaluation
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-582001",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Token-aggregation + prefetch: regression watch and robustness evaluation",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-02-22",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-10",
  "creator": "Ava Martinez",
  "assignee": "Rahul Patel",
  "project": "Inference-Config-Health",
  "cycle": "2026-W09",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-03-31",
  "labels": [
    "evals",
    "regression-monitoring",
    "serving-runtime",
    "kv-prefetch"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-611200",
    "ENG-574000"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "runtime-1.22",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Goal: Build a repeatable eval and monitoring harness that detects subtle quality regressions introduced by token-aggregation (microbatching/aggregation heuristics) and KV-prefetch policies. We want to understand the functional cost (response divergence, hallucination rate, structured-output integrity) per unit latency saved across representative production slices and ensure safe rollout rules for config changes. Background: Recent runtime work introduced an aggressive token-aggregation mode that reduces per-request overhead by merging short concurrent requests and a KV-prefetch heuristic that proactively warms KV caches for long-running chat sessions. Early perf gains are promising, but there are anecdotal degradations on structured tasks (code, JSON-extraction) and on certain prompt fingerprints. This ticket scopes an evaluation plan, orchestration for long-running watches, alert thresholds, and a canary gating policy for config rollouts.",
  "acceptance_criteria": "1) We can run a 10k-sample slice-based evaluation within CI that reports per-slice latency delta and quality regression scores for any candidate config change. 2) An alerting rule is defined that trips when weighted quality delta > 2% and latency improvement < 10% or when any structured-output integrity test fails. 3) Canary gating automation (deploy blocked/rollback) implemented in the rollout pipeline using the harness. 4) Dashboard widgets and a single-run report template are added to the perf dashboard.",
  "evaluation_metrics": "- latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, throughput_rps, avg_tokens_per_request\n- quality_emd (earth mover distance) on distribution of n-gram overlaps for freeform outputs\n- structured_integrity_pass_rate (JSON/CSV extraction tests)\n- hallucination_rate (precision/recall against reference KG)\n- semantic_similarity_mean (embedding cosine vs golden)\n- per-slice_weighted_regression_score (custom weighted delta)\n- stability_score (variance of outputs across repeated seeds)",
  "test_datasets": "- prod-sampled-10k (anonymized production traces covering web/chat/agent)\n- code-generation-promptset-1k (open-source)\n- structured-extraction-500 (forms + receipts)\n- conversational-long-context-2k\n- adversarial-prompt-fingerprints-200 (synthesized edge cases)",
  "methodology": "1) Baseline run: current stable config (runtime-1.21) across full dataset. 2) Candidate runs: token-aggregation at three aggressiveness levels and KV-prefetch enabled/disabled + two TTL settings. 3) For each run capture deterministic outputs by pinning model version & seed, collect latency traces with synthetic burst injection to emulate microbursts. 4) Compute per-slice metrics and produce a regression matrix (quality delta vs latency improvement). 5) Statistical significance: bootstrap per-slice with 1000 resamples; highlight regressions with p < 0.05 and effect size > threshold. 6) Produce human-review digest for any failing slices with example prompts and diffs.",
  "monitoring_playbook": "- Alert tier-1: structured_integrity_pass_rate drops by >1 percentage point for any slice -> page oncall infra.\n- Alert tier-2: per-slice_weighted_regression_score > 2% for >30min -> create auto-ticket and pause rollout.\n- Rollback rule: if any structured_integrity test fails OR global weighted quality delta >3% during canary -> immediate automatic rollback and notify SRE + PM.\n- Follow-up: if alert fires, run postmortem within 72 hours and quarantine failing prompt fingerprints into a protected testset.",
  "orchestration_and_harness": "- Integrate eval job into CI pipeline (github actions) that can be triggered by config PRs.\n- Long-running watches: scheduled job every 6 hours that runs lightweight sampled checks and reports to dashboard.\n- Canary gating: deployment job calls the harness with canary sample (1% traffic equivalent) and will auto-block if alerts fire.\n- Repro artifacts: store outputs, diffs, and metric snapshots in a date-stamped folder on GCS and link in report.",
  "artifacts": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Token+Aggregation+Prefetch+Study",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298",
    "https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/token-agg-prefetch-matrix"
  ],
  "checklist": [
    "seed evaluation harness and sample runner",
    "implement deterministic output capture (model version + seed)",
    "define per-slice weighting scheme with PM",
    "add structured-output unit tests",
    "add alerts to ops-monitoring",
    "hook canary gating into deploy pipeline",
    "write runbook for oncall"
  ],
  "risks_and_mitigation": "- Risk: Small but high-impact regressions on rare prompt fingerprints may be masked by global averages. Mitigation: enforce per-slice thresholds and maintain adversarial fingerprint set.\n- Risk: Increased monitoring load and storage. Mitigation: lightweight periodic checks + TTL on stored diffs.\n- Risk: Flaky CI due to nondeterministic model IO. Mitigation: pin seeds and run small ensemble to estimate variance.",
  "notes_or_decisions": "- Decided to prioritize structured-output integrity over marginal latency wins for enterprise tenants.\n- We will treat KV-prefetch toggles as separate binary feature flags to allow independent rollback.\n- Metric weighting will be: structured_integrity 40%, hallucination_rate 30%, semantic_similarity 20%, latency 10% (subject to PM signoff).",
  "comments": [
    "2026-02-23 Ava Martinez: Initial scope drafted; shared with PM and SRE for feedback.",
    "2026-02-26 Rahul Patel: Implemented deterministic capture prototype and small-run diffs; added synthetic microburst runner (PR linked).",
    "2026-03-02 Priya Kaur (PM): Reviewed slice weighting proposal; suggested raising structured-output weight to 40% \u2014 accepted.",
    "2026-03-06 Jin Park (SRE): Added alert thresholds and will add Grafana dashboard panels; requested retention policy for diffs.",
    "2026-03-10 Rahul Patel: Canary gating automation merged to staging; lightweight watch scheduled every 6 hours. Next: finalize CI integration and run full 10k baseline this week."
  ],

    "methodology",

    "orchestration_and_harness",
    "risks_and_mitigation",
    "notes_or_decisions",
    "comments"
  ],

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-46812\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Statistical validation suite for embedding + rerank regression detection\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"creator\": \"Maya Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Jonah Reyes\",\n  \"project\": \"embeddings-eval-suite\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-04-01\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"reranking\",\n    \"drift-detection\",\n    \"offline-metrics\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-41722\",\n    \"ENG-25467\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.22\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Build a statistically-grounded validation suite that produces daily quality scorecards for embedding and reranking endpoints, surfaces regressions with confidence intervals, and integrates with alerting and PR workflows. This suite will combine curated human-labeled corpora, stratified sampling for latency buckets, synthetic perturbations, and time-series drift detectors. Outputs: nightly scorecards, auto-created incidents when metric regressions exceed thresholds, and a small lightweight CLI to run local quickchecks before merging embedding/rerank model changes.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Nightly job produces a JSON scorecard with at least these metrics: MRR@10, nDCG@10, precision@1, recall@K, embedding distance calibration (cosine shift), and paired-significance p-value between current and baseline.\",\n    \"Scorecard includes latency stratification: p50/p90 token generation and end-to-end rerank latency per shard.\",\n    \"Automated alerts defined: threshold-based (absolute) and regression-based (relative with bootstrap CI) that create a ticket and post to #infra-embeddings when triggered.\",\n    \"CLI 'embed-validate quickcheck' runs a 200-sample smoke test in under 2 minutes and returns pass/fail and simple diffs for top-k rerank outputs.\",\n    \"Integration with PR process: a GitHub check that runs the quickcheck and attaches the scorecard link when embeddings/rerank config files change.\",\n    \"Dashboard in Console that shows historical metrics and drift decomposition by dataset slice and latency bucket.\",\n    \"Runbook for on-call: explanation of common false positives, how to rebaseline goldset, and steps to roll back model variants to a fallback.\",\n    \"Documentation page in Confluence with dataset stewardship guidelines and labeling rubric.\",\n    \"End-to-end tests for the nightly pipeline and a small synthetic perturbation suite to validate detectors.\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_plan\": [\n    \"Phase 1: Build canonical scorecard schema and nightly runner (batch Spark job -> scoring service) using existing embedding eval infra as a base.\",\n    \"Phase 2: Curate validation corpora: (a) small human-verified core set (2000 queries across domains), (b) stratified latency slices from production traces, (c) synthetic perturbation generators (typos, paraphrases, adversarial negation).\",\n    \"Phase 3: Instrument rerank endpoints to capture top-k outputs and token-latencies for sampled requests; store samples in S3 with tags for slice and model-variant.\",\n    \"Phase 4: Implement statistical tests: bootstrap CI for mean differences, paired Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney when appropriate, and Kendall/MRR correlation checks for rerank stability.\",\n    \"Phase 5: Alerting and automation: implement regression-detector lambda that compares yesterday vs baseline window and opens ENG tickets + posts Slack alerts. Integrate with GitHub checks for pre-merge quickchecks.\",\n    \"Phase 6: Observability and UX: Console dashboard + downloadable scorecard JSONs for auditors; add endpoints for programmatic polling (read-only).\",\n    \"Phase 7: Run internal pilot with two product teams for one month, iterate thresholds and onboarding docs, then promote to default nightly run for all embedding/rerank models.\"\n  ],\n  \"technical_considerations\": [\n    \"Sampling strategy must be cost-aware: use reservoir sampling on production traces to keep required sample set under budgeted S3/compute cost.\",\n    \"Latency-aware slices: bucket samples by observed inference p50/p90 to detect quality-latency tradeoffs introduced by new quantized variants.\",\n    \"Baseline management: support rolling baselines (30-day window) and per-model pinned baselines for release blockers.\",\n    \"False positive mitigation: require both absolute drop and statistically significant paired test before auto-creating high-priority incidents.\",\n    \"Data retention and PII: sampled request payloads must be redacted and follow Private deployment policy; store only tokens + hashed identifiers where necessary.\",\n    \"Performance: nightly job must complete within the 2-hour nightly window; quickcheck must be sub-2 minutes for developer feedback loop.\",\n    \"Cost: estimate additional monthly S3 + compute ~ $1.5k for the core suite initially; include budget in the infra cost center.\"\n  ],\n  \"risks_and_mitigation\": [\n    \"Risk: Over-alerting on minor variance leads to alert fatigue. Mitigation: use sliding windows and require CI overlap test before raising P1s.\",\n    \"Risk: Goldset stale or biased. Mitigation: implement quarterly goldset review with labelers and rotate in fresh queries from production sampling.\",\n    \"Risk: Increased storage and compute cost. Mitigation: aggressive retention policy and ability to downsample older runs to aggregated statistics only.\",\n    \"Risk: Inconsistent measurements across dedicated vs hosted. Mitigation: include environment tags and require separate baselines per deployment mode.\"\n  ],\n  \"deliverables\": [\n    \"Scorecard schema and nightly runner in repo 'infra/embed-eval'.\",\n    \"Embed-validate CLI with quickcheck command in 'tools/embed-validate'.\",\n    \"Console dashboard with historical graphs and dataset slice filters.\",\n    \"GitHub check integration and example workflow for PRs modifying models/config.\",\n    \"Confluence doc: 'Embedding & Rerank Validation Playbook' with stewarding guidelines.\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-01-12 - Maya Patel: Initial spike completed. Prototype scorecard schema in /repos/infra/embed-eval/schema/v1.json. Found that MRR variance is high on tail-heavy datasets.\",\n    \"2026-01-25 - Jonah Reyes: PoC runner done. It samples 5k requests from traces and computes MRR/nDCG. Needs latency tagging and CI computations.\",\n    \"2026-02-02 - Elisa Gomez (Data Science): Suggested adding stratified bootstrap to handle heavy-tailed relevance scores; shared notebook Gist: gist.github.com/elisa/stratified-bootstrap.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 - Jonah Reyes: PR 241 on GitHub opens for CLI quickcheck (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/241). Running quickcheck in CI has ~90s runtime on small samples.\",\n    \"2026-03-01 - Product review: PM Neil Chang requested a dashboard tile showing model-impact-by-customer-tier. We'll add a customer_tier slice to the scorecard.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 - Security: small note to ensure sampled request redaction for Private customers. Added retention plan and redaction checklist to the Confluence doc.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 - Jonah Reyes: Nightly runner scheduled in Airflow; first nightly run succeeded. Observed a small regression on a paraphrase-heavy slice; alert created and labeled P2 for triage.\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Validation+Playbook\",\n    \"GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/241\",\n    \"Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/embed-scorecard-proto\",\n    \"Notebook (analysis): https://gist.github.com/elisa/stratified-bootstrap\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"implementation_plan\",\n    \"technical_considerations\",\n    \"risks_and_mitigation\",\n    \"deliverables\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_055e17a2e9ad484b9aaef11f95ed2eeb\"\n}",

  "description": "Build a statistically-grounded validation suite that produces daily quality scorecards for embedding and reranking endpoints, surfaces regressions with confidence intervals, and integrates with alerting and PR workflows. This suite will combine curated human-labeled corpora, stratified sampling for latency buckets, synthetic perturbations, and time-series drift detectors. Outputs: nightly scorecards, auto-created incidents when metric regressions exceed thresholds, and a small lightweight CLI to run local quickchecks before merging embedding/rerank model changes.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Nightly job produces a JSON scorecard with at least these metrics: MRR@10, nDCG@10, precision@1, recall@K, embedding distance calibration (cosine shift), and paired-significance p-value between current and baseline.",
    "Scorecard includes latency stratification: p50/p90 token generation and end-to-end rerank latency per shard.",
    "Automated alerts defined: threshold-based (absolute) and regression-based (relative with bootstrap CI) that create a ticket and post to #infra-embeddings when triggered.",
    "CLI 'embed-validate quickcheck' runs a 200-sample smoke test in under 2 minutes and returns pass/fail and simple diffs for top-k rerank outputs.",
    "Integration with PR process: a GitHub check that runs the quickcheck and attaches the scorecard link when embeddings/rerank config files change.",
    "Dashboard in Console that shows historical metrics and drift decomposition by dataset slice and latency bucket.",
    "Runbook for on-call: explanation of common false positives, how to rebaseline goldset, and steps to roll back model variants to a fallback.",
    "Documentation page in Confluence with dataset stewardship guidelines and labeling rubric.",
    "End-to-end tests for the nightly pipeline and a small synthetic perturbation suite to validate detectors."
  ],
  "implementation_plan": [
    "Phase 1: Build canonical scorecard schema and nightly runner (batch Spark job -> scoring service) using existing embedding eval infra as a base.",
    "Phase 2: Curate validation corpora: (a) small human-verified core set (2000 queries across domains), (b) stratified latency slices from production traces, (c) synthetic perturbation generators (typos, paraphrases, adversarial negation).",
    "Phase 3: Instrument rerank endpoints to capture top-k outputs and token-latencies for sampled requests; store samples in S3 with tags for slice and model-variant.",
    "Phase 4: Implement statistical tests: bootstrap CI for mean differences, paired Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney when appropriate, and Kendall/MRR correlation checks for rerank stability.",
    "Phase 5: Alerting and automation: implement regression-detector lambda that compares yesterday vs baseline window and opens ENG tickets + posts Slack alerts. Integrate with GitHub checks for pre-merge quickchecks.",
    "Phase 6: Observability and UX: Console dashboard + downloadable scorecard JSONs for auditors; add endpoints for programmatic polling (read-only).",

# Agent Guidelines for Langfuse Langfuse is an open source LLM engineering platform for developing, monitoring, evaluating, and debugging AI applications. ## How To Work - Read the minimal local context required for the task. - Keep changes scoped and avoid unrelated refactors. - If you are about to write a `useEffect` — or sync fetched data into state, or wire form initial values from loaded data — read `.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md` first. Most such effects should not exist. - For bug fixes, write the failing test first, confirm it fails, then fix the bug. If the bug depends on a data shape, pause and ask: can `pnpm run seed` prefill that shape locally? If not, consider extending a seeder scenario so the bug stays cheaply reproducible (`packages/shared/scripts/seeder/AGENTS.md`), or note why a seed cannot express it. - For user-visible frontend changes in `web/**`, review the affected flow in a real browser before signoff. Prefill the data the flow needs with the seed CLI (`pnpm run seed -- list` shows scenarios; runs print UI deep links) — never with ad-hoc scripts or raw ClickHouse inserts. - When fixing an isolated styling issue in an individual component, read `.agents/skills/storybook/SKILL.md` create or update a component story following its guidance first. - Every PR auto-builds (via GitHub Actions) a disposable, full-stack preview at `pr-.preview.langfuse.com` — nothing to spin up. Use the `langfuse-previews` skill to use or debug one, e.g. read a preview's web/worker error logs with `kubectl`. - For documentation screenshots in Markdown, avoid fixed `height` on `` tags; prefer Markdown images or width-only HTML so previews preserve aspect ratio. - When working on the search bar or any filtering UI/grammar, read `web/src/features/search-bar/README.md` first. It owns the grammar ↔ `FilterState` contract, the validate/lower parity invariants, and the cross-view extension playbook — the bar is intended to become the primary filter interface for every filterable view, so new filtering work extends it through that contract rather than forking it. - When adding or modifying any chart, dashboard, or chart formatter, read `web/src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md` first — the charts manifesto. It owns the data → preparer → visualiser contract: presentation decisions live in the preparer, not the chart components. - Do not add or widen ESLint disable comments or config overrides without explicit user approval for the exact rule and scope. - Always quote file paths in shell commands, or use `noglob` for path-heavy commands, to avoid zsh glob expansion issues with dynamic Next.js routes. - Never invoke Node-installed binaries through `./node_modules/.bin/*`. Always run them through `pnpm`. - Never commit secrets or credentials. Keep `.env*.example` files in sync with required env vars. ## Project Structure ```text langfuse/ |- web/ # Next.js app (UI + tRPC + public REST) |- worker/ # Queue consumers and background processing |- packages/shared/ # Shared domain, DB, queue contracts, repositories |- ee/ # Enterprise package consumed by web |- generated/ # Generated API clients (do not hand-edit) |- fern/ # API definition sources `- scripts/ # Repo scripts ``` - Dependency direction: - `web` -> `@langfuse/shared`, `@langfuse/ee` - `worker` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/ee` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/shared` -> no imports from `web`, `worker`, or `ee` - Queue payload schemas and queue-name contracts are owned by `packages/shared/src/server/queues.ts`. - High-signal shared entry points: - Domain models: `packages/shared/src/domain/{observations,traces,scores}.ts` - Postgres schema: `packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma` - ClickHouse migrations: `packages/shared/clickhouse/migrations/{clustered,unclustered}/*.sql` - Architecture principles live in `.agents/ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES.md`. ## Core Commands - Install deps: `pnpm install` - Dev all packages: `pnpm run dev` - Dev web only: `pnpm run dev:web` - Dev worker only: `pnpm run dev:worker` - Lint all: `pnpm run lint` - Typecheck all: `pnpm run typecheck` / `pnpm tc` - Run a single test file (vitest filters on the filename argument): - web server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test ` (client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client `) - worker: `pnpm --filter worker run test ` - shared: `pnpm --filter @langfuse/shared run test ` - Build check: `pnpm run build:check` - Full build: `pnpm run build` - Worktree bootstrap: `bash scripts/codex/setup.sh` - Worktree maintenance: `bash scripts/codex/maintenance.sh` - Install Playwright Chromium: `pnpm run playwright:install` ## Local Data Inspection - For feature testing and debugging, inspect the local databases directly when it helps you understand the existing test data. Prefer read-only queries, and continue to use the seed CLI to create frontend test state rather than ad-hoc inserts. - Dev Docker Compose exposes these clients on `${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}`: - Postgres: `PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres}" psql -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${POSTGRES_HOST_PORT:-5432}" -U "${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}" -d "${POSTGRES_DB:-postgres}"` - ClickHouse: `clickhouse client --host "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" --port "${CLICKHOUSE_NATIVE_PORT:-9000}" --user "${CLICKHOUSE_USER:-clickhouse}" --password "${CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD:-clickhouse}" --database default` - Redis: `REDISCLI_AUTH="${REDIS_AUTH:-myredissecret}" redis-cli -h "${HOST_IP:-127.0.0.1}" -p "${REDIS_HOST_PORT:-6379}"` - If any connection fails, check `docker-compose.dev.yml` for local override variables and confirm the services are running. ## Verification - `web/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted web tests. - `worker/**`: `pnpm run lint` plus targeted worker tests. - `packages/shared/**` non-schema changes: `pnpm run lint` plus one targeted web check and one targeted worker check. - `packages/shared/prisma/**` or `packages/shared/clickhouse/**`: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run db:generate`, and targeted web/worker regressions. - Public API contracts in `web/src/pages/api/public/**`, `web/src/features/public-api/types/**`, or `fern/apis/**`: `pnpm run lint`, targeted server API tests, and Fern update/regeneration. - Cross-package refactors: `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`, and targeted tests for impacted packages. - Client-bundle soundness: CI scans every prod web build (`pnpm run scan:client-bundle`) for minifier-dropped bindings and Node-only globals leaking into browser chunks — the SWC dropped-binding class ships runtime-only `ReferenceError`s that dev builds and type checks cannot see (LFE-10645). On failure, `scripts/scan-client-bundle.mjs`'s header explains the canonical fix. End your turn with evidence, not claims: quote each check's summary line — e.g. `Tasks: 8 successful, 8 total` (turbo lint/typecheck) or `Tests 12 passed (12)` (vitest) — say which checks you skipped and why, never report unverified work as done, and never end with work pending. ## Generated Files Do not hand-edit generated or build artifacts: - `generated/*` - `web/.next/*` - `web/.next-check/*` - `*/dist/*` - `packages/shared/prisma/generated/*` Public API contract changes must update Fern sources in `fern/apis/**` and regenerated outputs. # Charts & Dashboards — Architecture Manifesto

> A short, opinionated statement of how charting works here and where it's going.
> Read this before adding a chart type, a formatter, or a dashboard.

## The goal

**Show _any_ data clearly.** Unknown shape, any time range or scale, one series or
two hundred, clean or noisy, sparse or overloaded — a chart should render it
legibly and consistently, and let a person _read_ it through interaction. We do
not special-case per chart. We build one adaptable pipeline and feed everything
through it.

## The one rule: one-way flow, two layers

```
   data  ──▶  PREPARE  ──▶  VISUALISE  ──▶  pixels
            (decide)        (render)
```

- **Prepare** owns every _decision_: parsing, units, date/number/duration
  formatting, colors, series order, legend summaries, top‑N, axis type, scale,
  null handling. Pure functions. No React. Unit-tested.
- **Visualise** owns _only rendering_: it maps a presentation-ready model onto
  the chart library and decides nothing. If a component is reaching back to
  reformat or re-derive, the decision is in the wrong layer.

Strictly one direction. The visualiser never re-decides what the preparer
resolved. (When the same value got formatted in three places, we got three
different — and sometimes wrong — dates. One source of truth per decision.)

## Principles — the "show whatever data" doctrine

1. **One normalized model is the pivot.** Every source lowers into a single
   typed, presentation-agnostic shape _once_, up front. Everything downstream
   targets that shape and never knows where the data came from.

2. **Decide presentation once, upstream.** Units, decimals, thresholds, colors,
   labels, and time format are resolved in the preparer into ready-to-render
   values. The renderer reads derived properties; it never re-derives them.

3. **Infer what the data didn't declare.** Assume input is under-specified and
   messy. Have a default for every missing piece — type from values, the time
   field, the bucket granularity (from spacing), series names from labels.

4. **Adapt to scale reactively, not predictively.** Don't compute "nice" ticks
   yourself — let the scale place them and _format the spacing you're given_.
   Pick number/date/duration formats by magnitude and granularity. Size axes by
   measuring labels, not guessing.

5. **Messy and overloaded is a first-class, _bounded_ case.** Bound cost at the
   source (≈ one point per pixel), not in the renderer. Cap unbounded series
   with an explicit, reversible limit (+ an "others" rollup where it's
   meaningful); never silently truncate without saying so.

6. **Null means something — say which.** Distinguish "no data here" (a gap)
   from "connect across" from "zero". Make the choice explicit; most
   "messy data looks wrong" bugs live in implicit null handling.

7. **Group by meaning, not position.** Series that share a unit share an axis;
   mismatched units earn a second axis — automatically, by derived key, so the
   layout adapts to an unknown number of series.

8. **Fail into guidance, not a blank box.** When data can't be drawn, detect
   _why_ (missing time field? no numeric field? empty?) and offer the next
   action.

9. **Interaction is readability.** Dense data is made legible by hovering,
   focusing, and a crosshair synced across a shared timeline — not only by
   throwing data away. Precise-on-hover beats sparse-by-default.

10. **Split "how to draw" from "what to draw."** Rebuild render config only when
    the structure changes; a new data tick should just swap arrays. Stable,
    memoized inputs; the heavy reconciliation happens rarely.

## Visual & interaction direction

> The architectural rules above say _where_ a decision lives. These say _what_ to
> decide when you draw. One stance underlies all of them: **the data carries the
> visual weight; the frame stays quiet.** Chrome — grid, axes, labels — is pushed
> to low contrast so series shape and color are what the eye lands on. High
> data-ink, always.

- **V1 — Draw what was measured; don't invent shape between points.** Straight
  segments by default. A smooth/spline curve _implies values that were never
  sampled_ — treat it as an explicit opt-in, not a prettifier. Use stepped lines
  only for hold-until-change (state/counter) data.

- **V2 — Missing is a gap, not a zero.** A null breaks the line. Bridge a gap
  only when the series semantically continues across it; never substitute `0` to
  "fill" a hole — that invents a measurement. Break the line when a gap exceeds
  the expected sampling cadence. Zero-fill is permitted only where stacking math
  needs a number. (This is principle 6, made visual.)

- **V3 — Encode certainty with one consistent grammar.** Less-trustworthy data —
  a still-aggregating final bucket, a comparison/previous period — renders
  _dotted and paled_, never dropped and never identical to confirmed data. One
  treatment, so a reader learns it once.

- **V4 — Hover reads a vertical slice, snapped to real samples.** The crosshair
  tracks the cursor, but the readout snaps to the nearest actual point — never a
  fabricated value at an arbitrary x. Near a gap the snap tolerance tightens so a
  tooltip never floats over emptiness.

- **V5 — Crosshair is shared across the timeline; the tooltip is the hovered
  chart's alone.** Charts on one time range share a single vertical time-marker;
  only the chart under the cursor opens a tooltip, listing every series at that
  instant, sorted by value, the focused one emphasized. Emphasis lives in the
  tooltip and the legend — the canvas stays calm. Dimming series _on the canvas_
  is reserved for one deliberate gesture (vertical proximity to a line) and must
  be flicker-free, never a side effect of ordinary hover.

- **V6 — Color is identity, assigned once.** A series' color is derived from the
  series and read back by the legend, so swatch and line can never diverge, and
  the same entity keeps its color across every chart. The palette is bounded; a
  colorblind-safe option exists.

- **V7 — Formatting is type-driven and adaptive — trust the scale.** Numbers,
  durations, bytes, percentages, currency, and dates each format by their kind
  and by the magnitude/granularity the scale chose; one common unit per axis.
  Tick precision follows the scale (don't truncate a narrow range); tooltip
  precision is capped for reading; digits are tabular so they don't jitter.

- **V8 — Bound the frame, not the data.** Cap drawn series at a legible top-N
  with an honest "N of M" (and an "others" rollup where it sums); bound the
  legend (scroll / "+N more"); bound density upstream (≈ one point per pixel).
  Never reach legibility by silently dropping data in the renderer.

## Where we are / where we're going

- **Now:** the visualiser is a set of recharts components behind one `Chart`
  dispatcher. Three preparer seams are in place: the **time axis**
  (`prepareTimeAxis` — raw timestamps in, granularity-adaptive labels out, one
  formatter for every chart), the **series cap** (`prepareVisibleSeries` —
  ranks a breakdown by magnitude and keeps the top‑N so a high-cardinality
  group-by of hundreds of series stays both legible and fast, with an honest
  "top N of M" note rather than a silent truncation; see principle 5), and
  **missing-cell semantics** (`prepareDenseSeries` — makes every
  (bucket, series) cell explicit: a real `0` for additive metrics, `null` — a
  visible gap — for non-additive ones, with `connectNulls` off by default so a
  line never draws across a no-data bucket; V2 made real, LFE-10694).
  The interaction direction (V4/V5) is largely in place: a synced vertical
  crosshair, a tooltip that opens only on the hovered chart, and a vertical
  proximity highlight.
- **Known visual debts** (drawn but not yet matching the direction above):
  series color is assigned by index and cycles every 8 rather than being a
  stable identity (V6) — a visualiser default to migrate into the preparer.
  (V1's smooth-by-default debt is paid: lines and areas draw straight
  (`type="linear"`) since LFE-10694.)
- **Next:** move the remaining decisions — series colors (V6), curve/interpolation
  opt-ins (V1), legend summaries, units, axis type & scale — out of the components and
  into the preparer, until the visualiser is purely presentational and the
  preparer is the single, tested place where "what should this look like" is
  answered.

The target: adding a new chart should mean teaching the **preparer** a new shape,
not teaching every component a new special case.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -euo pipefail

ensure_env_file() {
  local target_path="$1"
  local fallback_path="$2"

  if [ -f "$target_path" ]; then
    return 0
  fi

  cp "$fallback_path" "$target_path"
}

if ! command -v corepack >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "corepack is required. Use an environment with Node.js 24 support."
  exit 1
fi

corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@11.10.0 --activate

ensure_env_file .env .env.dev.example
ensure_env_file .env.test .env.test.example

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ! docker image inspect "langfuse-in-app-agent-sandbox:latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "packages/in-app-agent-sandbox-runtime/.local-image-built"
  fi

  pnpm turbo run build:docker-image --filter @repo/in-app-agent-sandbox-runtime --output-logs errors-only
else
  echo "Skipping local in-app agent sandbox image build because Docker is not available."
fi

# Install Chromium into the default user-level Playwright cache so frontend
# browser review works on first bootstrap.
pnpm run playwright:install

# Generate the shared Prisma client explicitly in the current worktree before
# the workspace-wide db:generate task, which may be satisfied by Turbo cache.
pnpm --filter=shared run db:generate

# Prisma client generation is needed for typecheck/build tasks.
pnpm run db:generate

item.text:
Resolved both Langfuse #15208 correctness bugs on `person/sana-farid`.

- Histogram: bins now use raw values and raw edges. Only labels are rounded, with adaptive precision ensuring distinct edges. Added the seven-bin `[0,1]` regression placing `0.857` in bin 6.
- Pivot: `avg_*` subtotals and totals now use count-weighted averages when a positive count metric is available. The tested fallback remains the legacy unweighted mean when it is unavailable. Non-average aggregations remain unchanged.

All six changed files were indexed: two implementations, two regression-test files, and both candidate notes. Individual branch diffs and the combined mounted personal-branch contents were verified.

Checks attempted:

- Histogram focused test: blocked before collection — `/bin/bash: pnpm: command not found`
- Pivot focused test: blocked before collection — `/bin/bash: pnpm: command not found`
- The environment also lacks Node/Corepack, so no executable test result is claimed.

Both task branches merged successfully. Chronos initially rejected the pivot merge after the histogram merge due to workspace conflict validation; recreating the pivot branch from the updated personal branch produced the same reviewed pivot-only diff and merged cleanly. Both task branches were then deleted, confirmed absent from branch status.
